issues.description: Filter '*.exe' for the conda executable path is Windows-only and will hide all valid executables on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: In confpage.py the file browser is created with filters='*.exe'. On macOS and Linux, conda/mamba/micromamba binaries have no .exe suffix (e.g., /opt/homebrew/bin/conda, ~/miniconda3/bin/conda). Users will see an empty file picker and cannot select a valid executable. The filter should be platform-aware (e.g., '*.exe' on Windows, '*' otherwise) or use a generic 'All files (*)' option.

issues.description: validate_conda's substring match for 'mamba'/'conda' in --version output is brittle and may accept unrelated binaries
issues.detail: validate_conda checks `tool in out.decode().lower()` for ['micromamba', 'mamba', 'conda']. Any executable whose --version output happens to contain one of these substrings (e.g., a wrapper script printing 'Anaconda Python' or any tool with 'mamba' in a banner) will pass validation. A stricter check would parse `<name> <version>` from the first line, or check that the output starts with one of the tool names. Additionally, the order of the list matters for the substring search but it does not matter for `in` membership, suggesting the author may have intended a startswith check.

issues.description: validate_conda swallows stderr and may hang or block on misbehaving executables
issues.detail: run_program(...).communicate() without a timeout will block indefinitely if the selected binary hangs or waits on stdin. Some conda-like tools print --version to stderr, and the call only decodes stdout (out), missing those. A timeout (e.g., 5s) and merging stderr would make validation robust. Also `out.decode()` assumes UTF-8 and will raise on non-UTF-8 output, which is then caught by the bare except — silently rejecting valid executables.

issues.description: Empty-string conda_executable path validates as True, which is misleading
issues.detail: validate_conda returns True when conda_executable == ''. This is presumably to allow clearing the field, but it conflates 'empty' with 'valid conda', which means the kernel-spec code path may later read an empty string and silently fall back. Either document this explicitly or have callers check for empty before calling validate_conda. The fallback logic in kernelspec.py already does `if not conda_exe` after reading the config, so the empty case may still error out at kernel start with the unhelpful message — fine, but worth making explicit.

issues.description: kernelspec.py does not re-validate the custom conda path before use
issues.detail: When `custom_conda` is enabled, the code reads `conda_path` from config and uses it directly without checking that the path still exists, is executable, or actually is a conda-like tool. A user could enable the option, set a path, then delete/move the binary; the kernel will fail downstream with a less actionable error. A defensive `validate_conda(conda_exe)` (or at least `os.path.isfile`) before use, with a clear error message pointing back to Preferences, would harden this path. The `conda_version` call later may surface this, but the error chain is less informative than a direct check.

issues.description: Default config value 'conda_path': '' is stored at module top-level config but never migrated; existing installs will pick it up via defaults
issues.detail: Adding a new default key to main.py config is standard, but Spyder typically bumps a CONF_VERSION when default schemas change so that user configs migrate. The diff does not show a version bump. If the framework auto-merges new defaults this is fine; otherwise users on existing configs may not see the new key.

issues.description: Side-effect setFocus() added to select_file may surprise other callers
issues.detail: create_browsefile.select_file now calls edit.setFocus() after setText. This is a global change to a shared widget helper used across the preferences system. The behavior change is small but could shift focus unexpectedly in other confpages that use create_browsefile (file paths in editor, runtime, project config, etc.). Worth a quick audit of callers to confirm none assume focus stays on the browse button.

issues.description: Error message references a UI path that may not match the actual menu hierarchy
issues.detail: The new error in kernelspec.py says 'Preferences > Python interpreter > Conda executable'. Verify the section name is exactly 'Python interpreter' (some Spyder builds label it 'Python Interpreter' with capital I). Mismatched casing in user-facing strings tends to confuse non-developers. Also the message dropped 'mamba or micromamba' lower-casing — minor but worth a quick consistency pass.

issues.description: create_browsefile signature change does not pass tip/alignment-dependent behavior to validation
issues.detail: The new validate_callback/validate_reason parameters are forwarded to create_lineedit. This is fine, but no test or doc update accompanies the signature change. Other callers of create_browsefile across the codebase will need to pass these as keyword args; positional ordering with status_icon already in the middle means future additions are fragile. Consider keyword-only parameters going forward.

issues.description: Inline style 'margin-left: 3px' is a presentational hack
issues.detail: conda_path.setStyleSheet('margin-left: 3px') hardcodes a layout offset to align the browse widget under the checkbox. This works but ignores Spyder's existing layout/indent helpers and won't scale with HiDPI. Prefer a QHBoxLayout with proper spacers or a stylesheet rule in the theme system.

issues.description: The conda path field is enabled/disabled but does not clear when disabled
issues.detail: Toggling 'custom_conda' off disables the line edit but preserves its value in config. When the user re-enables, the previous (possibly stale) path returns. This is arguably correct UX (remember last value) but worth confirming intent. If the intent is 'when off, ignore the value entirely', the kernelspec read of conda_path is already gated by custom_conda — so behavior is fine. Just flagging for review.

positions.position: Substring match on three names is a near-collision; should parse the version line and assert the tool name appears at the start or as the first token. Anything less risks accepting wrappers, shell aliases, or unrelated binaries that mention 'mamba' in their banner.

This is a preferences dialog validator, not a security boundary. A user pointing at a binary is opting in. A loose substring match minimizes false negatives (e.g., custom mamba forks, vendored builds) and the kernel will fail loudly later if the binary actually doesn't behave like conda. Ship it.

dissents.topic: Whether kernelspec.py should re-validate the custom path before use

positions.position: Always re-validate at the point of use. Configs persist, binaries move, environments change. A 100ms check before launching a kernel is cheap insurance against a confusing error chain.

Validation is the confpage's job. Duplicating it in kernelspec couples two layers and risks divergent rules. Trust the config invariant; if it's wrong, the existing 'conda_exe not found' error path catches it.

Spyder is cross-platform and conda users on macOS/Linux are the majority of the affected population (the issue #20357 was filed for non-standard install locations, very common on Unix). A Windows-only filter silently breaking the picker on Unix is a release blocker.
Power users can type the path directly into the line edit; the filter only affects the GUI picker. Annoying but not a true blocker — call it P1.
validate_conda should answer 'is this a valid conda executable' — '' is not, so return False. Conflating 'cleared' with 'valid' is a category error.
Returning True for empty avoids a spurious red-X on a freshly-opened blank field. The UI layer should signal 'empty is fine if custom_conda is off' rather than failing validation.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful escape hatch for users whose conda/mamba/micromamba lives outside PATH, addressing #20357. Architecturally it's clean: a new config key, a preferences widget, and a fallback in the kernelspec argv path. The main concrete bug is the '*.exe' file filter, which makes the GUI picker unusable on macOS and Linux — likely a blocker. Secondary concerns cluster around the validator: substring matching is too loose, there's no timeout on the subprocess call, stderr is ignored, and the empty-string case returns True. Minor concerns include the absence of re-validation at kernel-launch time, an inline stylesheet hack, and a focus-stealing side effect in the shared create_browsefile helper. Overall: ship after addressing the file-filter and validator hardening; the design is sound.
